narrative:
Your predicted probability of failing the final year is 36%, meaning roughly a one-in-three chance of not passing. In this process, that risk is high enough to require remedial courses. It is a warning, not a certainty.

The strongest reason for the fail prediction is your history of past class failures: you have three, while students who passed averaged none. That pattern outweighed the factors leaning in your favour. The second most influential factor is that you receive extra school support; this leans toward passing, even though such support is uncommon among passing students, so the model treats it as a protective signal. The third factor is that your guardian is your father, whereas most passing students’ guardian is their mother; this also leans slightly toward passing. These protective factors reduce the risk, but they do not cancel the strong concern raised by repeated past failures.

To improve, treat the remedial courses as a chance to break that repeated-failure pattern: attend consistently, ask for targeted help in subjects you have failed before, and make full use of the school support already available. Your zero absences and wish to continue to higher education are positive foundations to build on.
